ideas.title: The clay-pot cell: copper in its own blue salt
ideas.critique: It fixes the motor that would not turn, and the visible chemistry is new to the island: plate colour from Faraday's law, the blue thinning as Cu2+ runs out, the pot wall's resistance set by how it was fired. The risk is that the film is once more a fixed camera on a device left alone, so the payoff has to be the player adding pots and the motor answering, not a pot sitting there.

ideas.title: The motor turns the potter's wheel that throws its own cell pot
ideas.critique: The loop where the motor makes the pots that power it is a strong story, and Lumi's beak actually working the clay would be a body really doing something. It only works once the cells give real power, and a yield-stress ring pulled up for this one wheel is a rig with a single setup.

ideas.title: Hear the motor by its own current
ideas.nearest: Chipping a stone to change its note
ideas.critique: Sound driven by the solver's own torque ripple and commutation is a real step past the modal-note posts, and it is a new way to reach the watcher. But today the motor barely turns, so there is little to hear, and judging a build by ear is a diagnostic, not a game.

ideas.title: Sparks at the brushes in the dark
ideas.critique: Emissive arcs lighting copper at night play to the path tracer, and arc energy set by L i^2/2 is honest. Still, it is one more glowing thing lighting its surroundings, the spark's look will mostly be drawn rather than solved, and without current from real cells the sparks will be faint.

ideas.title: A windmill that charges lead plates
ideas.critique: State that builds over a day across sessions and gets spent at dusk is new to the island and is the heart of the big goal; the fizzing plates are something worth seeing. It is huge, and a dynamo with a lodestone stator will make almost nothing: if the numbers are honest it fails quietly, and if they are tuned it is a rig.

ideas.title: An iron horseshoe wound with copper
ideas.critique: It is the coil-in-the-iron-pegs scene again, this time where it works; saturation and the difference between series and shunt winding add real depth, and the stator is a part the cart needs. To a watcher, though, a magnet lifting scraps is the expected payoff.

ideas.title: The plank track over the soft sand
ideas.critique: Laying a limited stack of planks where the sand is softest is a real puzzle the physics answers, and it is a player verb rather than something watched. Planks on a Winkler foundation and ruts are solid but not surprising, and it needs a cart and pushers to show off.

ideas.title: First ride: no motor, just the dune
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Friends riding a runaway cart that digs in and slews is a moment people would share, and it is the first time riders' weight matters. But it is yet another object released down a slope with outcomes that differ by shape, and the friends are cargo, not actors.

ideas.title: One friend pulls the rope
ideas.nearest: Thin ice, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Giving every species a mass from its mesh is engine work that lasts, and a creature leaning into a rope with its feet creeping is the kind of body animation the island lacks. It stands or falls on the pose: if the lean and the foot slip are not driven by the statics, it is a pony pushed along a path.

ideas.title: Blue crystals from the green rock
ideas.critique: A days-long time-lapse of crystals growing faceted on a string is a new way things change on the island, and it supplies the cell's salt. For the player it is mostly waiting at a jar, and the faceted habit will likely be a chosen shape rather than grown.
